title: The lymphatic ring assay: a 3D-culture model of lymphangiogenesis
protocol: Sterilize a beaker containing a magnetic stirrer.
Heat the sterile stock agarose solution (1.5% type IV) in the microwave to liquefy.
Pour the heated agarose solution into a 100 mm culture dish (25 ml/dish).
Allow the culture dish to gel at 4 °C for at least 3 hours.
Kill the mouse by cervical dislocation.
Lay the mouse back down on the dissecting board and fix forelegs upwards and hind legs downwards with pins.
Surface-sterilize the skin using Norvanol D or proprietary compounds.
Remove the skin and sternum to allow direct access to the heart.
Suck about 1 to 1.5 ml of blood from the left ventricle of a still-beating heart with an insulin syringe.
Transfer collected blood into MiniCollect serum tubes.
Centrifuge the blood at 12,000g for 10 minutes.
Keep the supernatant at 4 °C until use.
Place an isofluran-soaked Tork paper in a bell-jar and keep it closed to saturate its atmosphere.
Place a dish onto the paper to support the mouse to avoid direct contact with the isofluran.
Sterilize instruments by immersing them in Norvanol D or proprietary compounds.
Kill the mouse by beheading after making animals unconscious in the saturated-Isofluran bell-jar.
Lay the mouse back down on the dissecting board and fix forelegs upwards and hind legs downwards with pins.
Surface-sterilize the skin with Norvanol D or proprietary compounds.
Cut the skin along the abdominal midline and along the left and right anterior sides of the rib cage.
Open the sternal plate and cut ribs, leaving the diaphragm intact.
On the caudal side of the rib cage, cut the esophagus and vena cava to remove all thoracic organs with sterile scissors and forceps.
Fill rib cage with sterile PBS; wash out the blood with sterile gauze pads if needed.
Dissect carefully the periaortic fibroadipose tissue with very thin Norvanol-dry microdissection forceps under a binocular microscope (magnification 12X).
Break carefully the fat beneath the lymphatic duct.
Remove the surrounding fat from the lymphatic duct.
Clean the lymphatic duct thoroughly.
Cut the edges of the cleaned duct with Vannas scissors.
Transfer the cut duct to a culture dish containing penicillin/streptomycin supplemented ice-cold DMEM culture medium.
Prepare agarose cylinders using a 17-mm diameter puncher.
Punch the center of each cylinder with a 10-mm diameter puncher.
Remove the inner agarose piece from the punched cylinders.
Transfer four agarose cylinders to an 86x12 bacterial Petri dish.
Mix collagen R, 10x MEM, NaHCO₃, and NaOH on ice to adjust pH to 7.4.
Keep mixing the collagen mixture on ice during the experiment with a moderate magnetic stirrer rotation speed (100 rpm).
Add 150 μl of the collagen solution in each agarose cylinder.
Allow the collagen to polymerize for 10-20 minutes at 37°C.
Prepare lymphatic thoracic duct pieces during collagen polymerization.
Transfer the lymphatic thoracic duct into a Petri dish with a 50% (vol/vol) DMEM/collagen mix.
Unfold and cut the duct transversally into about 1 mm-long pieces.
Cover the pieces immediately with 50% (vol/vol) DMEM/collagen mix to maintain wetness.
Cut the duct in a Petri dish filled with DMEM using sterile microdissection forceps and Vannas scissors.
Ensure that all pieces are of approximately the same length.
Transfer duct pieces to each previously polymerized collagen gels in agarose cylinder using sterile microdissection forceps.
Soak briefly duct pieces in a mix of 75% vol/vol DMEM/collagen if option B was chosen in step 20.
Allow the duct pieces to fix to collagen in the agarose cylinder by incubating dishes at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Add 150 μl of collagen solution over the ducts and allow it to polymerize for 10 to 20 minutes at 37°C.
Add 6 ml of supplemented MCDB131 medium to the culture.
For assay using stimulators of lymphangiogenesis, add 4% Ultroser G to the culture medium.
For assay using inhibitors of lymphangiogenesis, add 10% FCS to the culture medium.
For assay using transgenic mice, use 3% autologous mouse serum isolated as explained at step 3.
Maintain cultures at 37°C in a humidified water-jacketed incubator under reduced oxygen conditions (5% O2, 5% CO2, and 90% N2) for 7 to 14 days.
Observe rings with a phase contrast microscope after 7, 9, or 11 days of culture.
Harvest lymphatic rings from the agarose cylinder and transfer them to PBS for a wash of 1 hour.
Fix washed lymphatic rings with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol/H2O or 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 minutes depending on the antibody to be tested.
Wash the lymphatic rings to be used for immunostaining with PBS for three rounds of 20 minutes at 50 rpm on an orbital shaker.
Block unspecific sites with 1.5% BSA-3% powder milk for 1 hour at room temperature at 50 rpm on an orbital shaker.
Incubate the lymphatic rings with primary antibody diluted in 0.15% BSA/0.3% powder milk/PBS.
Wash the lymphatic rings four times for 15 minutes each with PBS.
Incubate lymphatic rings with the appropriate fluorochrome-conjugated secondary antibody as per the initial antibody incubation protocol.
Wash the lymphatic rings four times for 15 minutes each with PBS.
Mount the lymphatic rings on a microscope slide with Vectashield-propidium iodide or DAPI mounting medium.
Fix the lymphatic rings with 4% formaldehyde for 1 hour before transferring them to 70% ethanol/H2O overnight.
Transfer specimens alternatively in a 95% (vol/vol) ethanol/H2O for two baths of one hour each.
Transfer specimens to isopropanol for two baths of one hour each.
Transfer specimens to xylene for two baths of one hour each.
Immerse specimens in paraffin overnight, starting with a first bath at 56°C for one hour.
Continue the paraffin process with a second bath at 56°C for one hour.
Section paraffin blocks at 5 μm on a microtome.
Place sections on Superfrost Plus slides laid on a 40°C plate to dry.
Perform usual immunohistochemistry.
